entities.name: Donatien Mahele Lieko Bokungu
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Donatien "Marc" Mahele Lieko Bokungu, a formidable Zairean general, served as the final army chief under President Mobutu Sese Seko, his career culminating in the dramatic collapse of the Zairean state during the First Congo War (1996-1997). A veteran of numerous internal conflicts and a loyalist to Mobutu's regime for decades, Mahele was thrust into command in 1996, tasked with defending a disintegrating nation against the rapidly advancing Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) led by Laurent-Désiré Kabila, backed by Rwanda and Uganda.

Promoted to Lieutenant-General and Chief of Staff of the Zairean Armed Forces (FAZ) in the face of imminent invasion, Mahele attempted to reorganize a demoralized and ill-equipped military. He was instrumental in the defense of key cities such as Kisangani and Mbuji-Mayi, though his efforts were ultimately overwhelmed by the AFDL's superior strategy and external support. Despite his reputation as a professional soldier and a reformer, Mahele struggled to overcome the deep-seated corruption, lack of discipline, and tribal divisions that plagued the FAZ, which had been systematically weakened by Mobutu himself to prevent potential coups. His command during the final months of the regime saw a desperate, often chaotic, struggle against an unstoppable tide.

Mahele's death on May 16, 1997, just days before Kinshasa fell to the AFDL, signaled the definitive end of Mobutu's 32-year rule and the Zairean state itself. His efforts, though ultimately unsuccessful in preserving the regime, underscored the profound internal fragilities that contributed to Zaire's collapse and the subsequent establishment of the Democratic Republic of Congo. His final stand against the AFDL became a symbol of a lost cause, marking a pivotal transition in Central African history and the violent reconfiguration of regional power dynamics.
